description: Use this when somebody wants a music visualiser or music visualisation (visualizer, visualization, musicviz, audio-reactive visuals): it writes a GLSL vibescape and returns a live link to it. The link draws and animates the vibescape in a browser, so it works for anybody who opens it, with or without the app. The vibescape is not in the public gallery until `share_vibescape` is called on it. The answer carries the id and the capability (`editKey`) that `share_vibescape` needs — keep it, because there is only one copy of it. Call `vibescape_reference` first for the uniforms and helpers the language has — a vibescape that ignores the music will look like a still image, and there is a linter that says so.

author.description: Who to credit it to. Leave it empty and it is credited to Minith Labs.

code.description: The vibescape: a GLSL function `vec3 render(vec2 p, float t)`. `p` is the position across the screen, centred on 0,0, and `t` is time in seconds. Return the colour as three numbers from 0 to 1. Read the music through the uniforms — uBass, uLevelSmooth, uBeatStrength, uScroll — or the picture will not move with the sound.

name.description: What to call it. A few words that say what the picture looks like.

name: create_vibescape
title: Create a vibescape
